Background and definitions Clinical severe infection is defined by WHO as one or more of the following clinical signs in infants aged 0–59 days: not feeding well, movement only when stimulated, high body temperature (≥ 38 °C), low body temperature (< 35.5 °C), and/or severe chest indrawing. An additional sign of clinical severe infection in infants aged 0–6 days is fast breathing (≥ 60 breaths per minute) (27, 28).
